story.value: The name beryllium comes from the Greek word beryllos, meaning beryl, which is a gemstone in which beryllium is found.
In 1828, the French chemist Antoine-Alexandre-Brutus Bussy and, independently, the German chemist Friedrich Wöhler first separated beryllium.
Beryllium was once also known as glucinium, from the Greek word glykys for sweet, until IUPAC chose the name beryllium in 1949.

uses.value: Beryllium is used to make windows for X-ray tubes.
Beryllium is used to make an alloy called beryllium copper, which is used for things such as springs and electrical contacts.
Beryllium is used in parts of the space shuttle, such as the windshield frame and brake discs.
Beryllium is used in things such as gyroscopes and computer parts.
